── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 42, 46, 34, 41 mi
This week: 12 mi over 3 runs.
Body: "Legs came back by Thursday. Blister healed."
Feeling: "Itching to train again."
Asks: "I feel ready. Can I go back to 40 miles next week and start speedwork for the 10K?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: Nice job sticking to the recovery week; now hold the easy pattern and nudge volume up gently rather than jumping to 40 miles and speedwork. …
Answers: (1) Not quite yet. … (2) Here is what I would do instead: this week around 20 to 24 mi with four easy runs and a few short strides, next week step toward 30 mi and… (3) Before I write that next block, tell me what you actually want to race. …
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full day off to keep stacking recovery after the marathon.
Tue: easy, 4 mi, conversational, heart rate under 140. Ease back into the week.
Wed: easy, 5 mi, add 4 x 20 seconds strides at the end on flat ground, full walk…
Thu: easy, 3 mi, very relaxed. Keeps the week flowing on tired legs.
Fri: rest. Protect Saturday and Sunday.
Sat: easy, 4 mi, flat and conversational. Primes Sunday.
Sun: easy, 7 mi, steady, heart rate under 145. First small step back toward a longer run.
